# Build plan — closed-slice history

> The archived record of every closed (✅) slice from the [build board](plan.md), moved here verbatim with its retrospective status paragraphs: the walking-skeleton milestones (M0–M6; M6 stands deferred with its 2026-07-08 note), the skeleton close-out and the Phase 7 QA batch, then Slices A, A2 and A2.1–A2.6. This file is precedent, not a board — nothing here is open; read it when a past slice's shape or an honest deviation matters, not by default. **Standing convention: when a slice closes (✅) on the board, its block moves here in the same commit.**

---

| # | Ticket | Deps |
|---|--------|------|
| T-001 | **Monorepo scaffold** — pnpm + Turborepo + `tsconfig.base.json`; empty packages per repo-structure (`contracts`, `db`, `model`, `data`, `knowledge`, `orchestration`, `capabilities`, `workflows`, `governance`, `ui`) and apps (`api`, `web-consultant`); dependency rules enforced (surfaces → `contracts`/`ui` only). | — |
| T-002 | **CI pipeline** — build, typecheck, lint, test on every PR; a failing dependency-rule check fails the build. | T-001 |
| T-003 | **`packages/db` substrate** — Postgres + pgvector via docker-compose for dev; migration tooling; connection/config plumbing. | T-001 |
| T-004 | **Migration: Drawer 1 (parties & access)** — Organisation, User (`external_identity` nullable), Project, Membership (one owner per project enforced), Participant. | T-003 |
| T-005 | **Migration: Drawer 2 (documents)** — Container, Version (append-only), **Sandbox document** (mutable by design, per the 2026-07-04 decision). | T-004 |
| T-006 | **Migration: Drawer 3 (work & execution)** — Work item, Conversation (`surface`, nullable `work_item_id`), Run (`parent_run_id`), Step (`parent_step_id`, `source_set`, `rail_outcomes`, model/tokens/cost) — all append-only. | T-004 |
| T-007 | **Migration: Drawers 4–5 (AI output & review)** — Suggestion (`sandbox_document_id`, `kind`, nullable `anchor` — the per-item ruling, 2026-07-06), Citation, Signal (append-only); DRR, Comment (thin). | T-005, T-006 |
| T-008 | **Append-only enforcement + tests** — DB-layer triggers: Version, Signal, Comment strictly insert-only; Run and Step immutable **once finished** (ADR-0028 §3) — UPDATE permitted only on `state`/`status`/`ended_at` while the row is `running`, DELETE never; tests prove content columns are immutable always and that any write to a completed/failed Run or Step is rejected. | T-007 |
| T-009 | **`packages/contracts` seed** — the types and endpoint schemas from [contracts.md](contracts.md), exported as the single source of truth; `apps/api` skeleton serving them (empty handlers). | T-001 |
| T-010 | **`packages/model` Router + two adapters** — the Router interface; an Anthropic **chat** adapter and a separate **embeddings** adapter (Voyage AI or equivalent — Anthropic exposes no embeddings API) behind it; model ids/versions surfaced for the Step audit fields. | T-001 |
| T-011 | **Seed script** — two Organisations (owner + member), one Project, Memberships, a consultant Participant (member org) and an owner Participant, **plus the wall-test subjects: one member-org User with no Participant, and a third Organisation with no Membership at all** (T-022/T-073 need them to exist); **one Work item** (`document_production`, titled, assigned to the consultant Participant, status in production — the governed-work anchor for M3–M5); and a small library: ~6 live `Container`/`Version` rows (`in_library`, `state = live`) with realistic content to draft from, plus one superseded version (to prove exclusion). | T-007 |
| T-012 | **Ingestion & embedding pipeline (`packages/data`)** — chunk seed Versions, embed via the Router, store vectors in pgvector beside the relational rows; embedding model id/version pinned per index (ADR-0024). | T-010, T-011 |
| T-083 | **Config, secrets & bootstrap** — typed env schema validated at boot, `.env.example`, model API keys and DB URLs per app; the first-day contributor path documented (clone → docker compose → migrate → seed → run). | T-003 |

## M1 — The access spine

| # | Ticket | Deps |
|---|--------|------|
| T-020 | **Access resolution predicate (`packages/governance`)** — `(organisation, participant, project) → entitled slice`: membership check, per-deliverable visibility (owner / author / shared), the hard subset invariant (ADR-0015). A pure, unit-tested function of the data — the wall. | T-011 |
| T-021 | **Skeleton session auth** — `POST /auth/session` + httpOnly cookie for the seeded users, `GET /me` (see the auth decision above). | T-009 |
| T-023 | **API-boundary enforcement** — requester resolution middleware on every request, deny-as-404 semantics, the error envelope (contracts §4); no endpoint accepts caller-supplied identity. | T-021, T-020 |
| T-022 | **Negative tests: the wall on the native surface** — the seeded no-Participant user and third-org user resolve to nothing on every endpoint; proves there is no code path admitting a scope the predicate did not. | T-023 |

## M2 — The Context gateway

| # | Ticket | Deps |
|---|--------|------|
| T-030 | **Assembly gateway signature (`packages/knowledge`)** — `assemble(request, environment, requester)` exactly as contracts.md §1; access resolution (T-020) runs inside the call; guiding/informing pipelines present but returning empty. | T-020, T-009 |
| T-031 | **Grounded pipeline: hybrid library retrieval** — vector similarity + lexical code/metadata match over the requester's entitled slice only; live-state filter (superseded/withdrawn excluded, one live version per container) as SQL pre-filters, not post-filters (ADR-0022/0024). | T-012, T-030 |
| T-032 | **v1 merge + channel annotation** — grounded-first concatenation within a fixed token budget, drop lowest-priority channel first; every returned item carries channel + source identity (ADR-0029 §5). | T-031 |
| T-033 | **Gateway wall tests** — same query, entitled vs unentitled requester: content vs nothing; the superseded Version never returned; no parameter exists to widen scope (signature-level test); the response is annotated by channel. | T-032 |

## M3 — The orchestrated run (the heart)

| # | Ticket | Deps |
|---|--------|------|
| T-040 | **Run/Step writer (`packages/orchestration`)** — Conversation/Run/Step lifecycle against the append-only tables; the run tree (`parent_run_id`/`parent_step_id`); state transitions running → completed/failed. | T-008, T-009 |
| T-041 | **The coded chain** — `retrieve → draft → ground-check → cite` as a fixed code spine (ADR-0027 §6, ADR-0028 §5); each step writes its Step row with full audit fields as it runs. | T-040 |
| T-042 | **`retrieve` leaf + the retrieval sub-agent** — baseline assembly via the gateway; one child Run doing targeted retrieval mid-chain (exercises `parent_run_id`/`child_run_id`); no store access except through `assemble()`. | T-041, T-032 |
| T-043 | **`draft` leaf (grounded generation, `packages/capabilities`)** — the one thinking leaf: prompt assembled from the working input, model called via the Router, draft produced with claim→source markers for the verifier. | T-041, T-010 |
| T-044 | **`ground-check` verifier** — deterministic doing leaf: every claim resolves to a source in the step's `source_set` or is withheld; withholding recorded in `rail_outcomes`. | T-043 |
| T-045 | **`cite` resolution + Suggestion write** — citations attached to grounded sources only; Suggestion(s) written with `kind`, content, rationale, citations, `sandbox_document_id` (the skeleton emits one unanchored `insert` per run — the per-item/anchor model is in the schema, ruled 2026-07-06). | T-044 |
| T-046 | **Run endpoints live (`apps/api`)** — `POST /conversations`, `POST /conversations/:id/runs`, `GET /runs/:id`, work-item endpoints; the full chain callable over HTTP; run reads scoped per the 2026-07-06 visibility ruling (work-item-bound → owner-readable; ad-hoc → requester's organisation only, deny-as-404 otherwise). | T-042, T-045, T-023 |
| T-047 | **M3 acceptance test** — the chain runs the same order every time; unsupported claims withheld; every surviving claim cites a live Version; the Run/Step tree is complete, immutable, with both defensibility fields populated; the sub-agent appears as a real child Run. | T-046 |

### Parallel tracks

Sequential spine: **T-001 → T-003/T-009 → migrations → T-020 → T-030 → T-041 → T-046 → T-082 → T-053 → T-080.** Off the spine, these run concurrently: T-010 (model), T-002 (CI), T-083 (config/bootstrap) and T-049 (UI tokens from the mockups) from day one; T-050/T-051 (scaffold + sandbox surface) once contracts and the skeleton auth exist (T-009/T-021 — shell work can begin earlier against a stubbed session), well before M3 completes; T-084 (e2e harness) beside M4; T-085 then T-070 (Copilot enablers + manifest) once T-046 is stable; T-012 (ingestion) beside M1.

**UI track:** the visual spec lives in `docs/design/mockups/` — eight Legora-clean screens (third cut, 2026-07-06: workspace landing, project home, Ask chat, Editor with chat + suggestion panel, foldered library, sandbox, review, owner run-audit), restructured to the owner's wireframes and the surfaces-alignment rulings (grill tracker session record), benchmarked on the observed Legora UI review ([docs/reference/legora-ui-review.md](../reference/legora-ui-review.md)). The project nav is Home · Ask · Editor · Documents · Review · Sandbox · Tools · History (Workflows renamed Tools, T-109; History added, T-108); Knowledge is staged with the moat slices (component 8 §6). The alignment session is closed (all items ruled 2026-07-06 — grill tracker session record). Post-skeleton screens (DRR/PDF review, plan builder, portfolio, add-in pane) are mocked when their slice starts.

## Slice A — Document management: the controlled lifecycle *(ticketed 2026-07-18)*

> **Status: ✅ built, T-113–T-129 all landed 2026-07-18** (one autonomous session; every ticket its own verified commit, CI green throughout). The T-129 acceptance suite drives the whole journey: plan → consolidate/confirm → draft → freeze → org-private internal QA → promote the QA-accepted frozen version → rounds/comments/codes → issue → respond → v2 → accept → library + grounding; plus the rejected pathway and the wall negatives. **Honest deviations & follow-ups:** review reads happen against the frozen version's text with the PDF rendition downloadable — the in-PDF anchored viewer (pdf.js) is the noted follow-up; the internal cycle launches when the freeze container carries a confirmed lead reviewer (no separate launch endpoint); drawer-5 comments landed as the `review_comments` table (clearer beside `sandbox_comments`); T-123/T-124/T-126's API halves shipped in one commit and their surfaces in T-127's cycle page; transmittal "notifies recipients" is a recorded fact, not delivery (the parked notification model); post-acceptance promotion opens a new revision cycle (pinned in tests); office→PDF conversion for uploads waits on the infra converter.

*Design session closed 2026-07-18 → ADRs 0032 (two-scope role-agnostic cycle), 0033 (per-org plans, appointment grants, administration), 0034 (canonical format, renditions); the data model's Drawers 1/2/3/5 are the table spec. Mockups for the new surfaces (plan builder, DRR table, PDF review) are drawn per-ticket as each surface starts, benchmarked on the ProjectWise friction map (docs/reference) — "no wizard" is the standing acceptance test for promote and freeze. The T-112 participants endpoint widens to the project roster per ADR-0033 (in T-117).*

## Slice A2 — Producing-side surfaces: the TIDP page, the sandbox drawer, bind & the multiplayer thread (prototype) *(ticketed 2026-07-23)*

> **Status: ✅ built, T-145–T-162 all landed 2026-07-23** (one session; each ticket its own verified commit — typecheck 13/13, db 21, api 116, governance 34, contracts 5, orchestration 13, e2e 33 green throughout). The producing-side deliverable lifecycle as **interactive surfaces** — turning the Slice A mechanical spine (T-113–T-129) and the ADR-0035 acknowledgement gate (T-134–T-138) into a browser-drivable prototype a consultant can actually walk. **One full-lifecycle slice** (owner-chosen 2026-07-23): TIDP page + schema → sandbox drawer + folders → create/bind documents → collaborate (shared thread + attached-source working set) → launch internal review from the folder view → freeze → promote → transmittal → acknowledgement. Multiplayer ships as **shared-thread visibility now, real-time presence/sync deferred** (owner-chosen). "No wizard" held for bind, freeze and promote. **Honest deviations & follow-ups:** `sandbox_documents.sandbox_id` stays nullable (the create path sets it, but the old implicit-org path remains) — NOT NULL when every write is wired; the sandbox drawer shows all the org's documents (filtered to a sandbox when one is selected); the T-162 acceptance stops at bind (promote-to-accept is the Slice A path, T-129); an owner→org transmittal/acknowledgement is exercised at the API level (T-137/T-161), the e2e drives the producing-side chain; real-time multiplayer presence deferred; super-user tier still T-133.

*Design session closed 2026-07-22 (producing-side-lifecycle grill) → ADRs 0036 (sandbox participant-scope model), 0038 (bound/unbound + the binding transition + metadata split), 0039 (multiplayer document collaboration), plus refinements to 0022 (attached-source working set) and 0032 (internal-cycle initiation, auto-freeze). Mostly a surfaces slice on existing mechanics; new backend only where session B added it. Mockups drawn per-ticket, benchmarked on the ProjectWise friction map and SharePoint for the sandbox drawer.*

**Slice A2.1 — Real interfaces (the producing-side UI, done properly)** — ✅ **ticketed and built 2026-07-24 (T-163–T-167).** Slice A2 proved the mechanics but shipped substandard UI: `window.prompt()` browser dialogs, emoji-as-icons, a nonexistent `.input` CSS class, no real TIDP builder, no metadata editors, and bound documents you couldn't see or navigate. This slice replaces that with best-in-class interfaces grounded in the design system (design-rules.md §A–§G), the ProjectWise/AssetWise friction map (file/metadata separation kept; "No Wizard", auto-surfaced attributes, safe basic ops — B1/B3/B4), and the Legora + ISO-19650-CDE register pattern (an editable deliverable register, a detail/metadata side-panel, searchable combobox pickers). **No `window.prompt`, no emoji-icons, elevation-4 modals, semantic tokens only** are the standing acceptance tests.

- **T-163 — UI foundation: Modal + form controls.** A `Modal` primitive (elevation-4 overlay, focus-trap, ESC/backdrop close, header/body/footer) and form controls (`Field`, `TextInput`, `TextArea`, `SelectInput`, `Combobox` searchable picker) in `@infora/ui` with CSS from the tokens and a component test. Retires `window.prompt` and the phantom `.input` class.
- **T-164 — The deliverable register (TIDP builder).** The Plan page becomes an editable register grid; "New deliverable" opens a proper modal form — the code-builder as live field dropdowns composing a preview reference, plus title/discipline/authoring metadata — "No Wizard". A row opens a detail panel.
- **T-165 — The bind dialog + bound-document visibility.** A modal with a **searchable combobox of the org's accessible unbound TIDP rows** (code + title) replaces the prompt; bound documents show their code and link to the deliverable, and the register shows each row's bound draft.
- **T-166 — Metadata editors (library + sandbox).** A metadata detail panel: container identity (read-only) + authoring metadata (editable, container PATCH); sandbox-document authoring metadata editable via an extended sandbox PATCH — grouped fields, real controls (file/metadata separation, B4 auto-surfaced attributes).
- **T-167 — Replace remaining prompts + emoji-icons; verify.** Convert the other prompt sites (sandbox create, folder, scope grant, working-set pin, transmit, acknowledge) to modals/forms; swap emoji glyphs for Lucide; update the e2e; full verification.

**Slice A2.2 — Hardening & follow-through** — ✅ **ticketed and built 2026-07-24 (T-168–T-175).** Closes the gaps flagged after A2.1: accessibility of the new primitives, lint hygiene, dark mode, the deferred deviations, and the two bigger deferred items (the elevated tier, real-time presence).
- **T-168 — Primitive accessibility (design-rules §D).** `Combobox` gets keyboard navigation (↑/↓/Enter/Escape) and `aria` roles; `Modal` gets a real focus-trap and focus-restore on close.
- **T-169 — Lint clean.** Run `pnpm check` (deps + lint + typecheck + tests) and clear anything it flags on the Slice A2/A2.1 code.
- **T-170 — Dark-mode pass.** Render the new modals/forms/register/sandbox in dark and fix any token gaps (design-rules §G item 1).
- **T-171 — `sandbox_documents.sandbox_id` → NOT NULL.** Backfill any nulls, make the create paths always set it, tighten the column.
- **T-172 — Humanise status labels.** A shared work-item-status label map (`in_production` → "In production") used by the register, sandbox and work-item surfaces.
- **T-173 — Register row detail panel.** A slide-over showing a deliverable's dates, reviewers and authoring team beside its metadata.
- **T-174 — The elevated (super-user) tier (T-133 realised).** A server-side gate for destructive lifecycle actions (close-reject, supersede, withdraw), surfaced only to elevated participants; reconciled with the org admin (ADR-0033) and ADR-0016's owner/member collapse.
- **T-175 — Real-time multiplayer presence (first cut).** A presence layer — who is viewing/editing a document — as the first concrete step of ADR-0039's deferred real-time half (heartbeat + read; live avatars in the editor), short of a full CRDT sync engine.

**Slice A2.3 — Classes of user + plan/scheme polish** — ✅ **ticketed and built 2026-07-24 (T-176–T-178)**, from owner feedback. Turns T-174's flat `elevated` flag into named **classes of user** and gates the plan/scheme surfaces on them. Design captured in `grill-sessions/prompt-user-classes.md` (removed 2026-08-04; in git history).
- **T-176 — Classes of user (capability matrix).** Derive the class from `(membershipRole × elevated)` — **owner super-user** / **guest super-user** / **ordinary** — no new stored role (doesn't reopen ADR-0016). Governance capability predicates (`canEditPlan`, `canEditScheme`, `canProposeScheme`); gate the plan create/patch API on super-user (editing the TIDP now requires it), the scheme PUT on owner-super, propose on guest-super; expose the class to the UI via /me.
- **T-177 — Clear "Edit coding scheme" button + role-aware surfaces.** Replace the hidden link with a prominent button; the schema page is fully editable by the owner super-user, propose-only for the guest super-user, view-only otherwise; the plan hides "New deliverable"/metadata-edit from non-super-users.
- **T-178 — Remove the redundant discipline free-text.** The New-deliverable modal keeps the scheme's discipline **dropdown** (when present) and drops the standalone "Discipline (optional)" free-text box.

**Slice A2.4 — Sandbox structure, freeze & versioning** — ✅ **built 2026-07-25**, from owner feedback on the sandbox surface. Prompt in `grill-sessions/prompt-sandbox-structure.md` (removed 2026-08-04; in git history).
- **T-179 — Sandbox folder-tree UI (SharePoint-shaped).** The flat sandbox table becomes a nested folder tree: folders nest and documents live *inside* their folder, with expand/collapse, a current-folder breadcrumb, and re-filing by drag-and-drop **or** the keyboard-accessible Move dialog (the `/folders/:id/move` + `/sandbox-documents/:id/move` endpoints already existed, T-153; a move never changes access, only where a document sits — ADR-0036). Fixed a latent gap: the vite dev proxy didn't forward `/sandboxes`, `/folders`, or `/sandbox-scope-grants`, so the browser's folder calls hit the SPA fallback — the first e2e (sandbox-tree.spec) to exercise them surfaced it. `Button` gained an `aria-label`/`title` passthrough so per-row "Move" buttons carry their row's context for a screen reader. *(Honest deviation: drag-and-drop is the mouse enhancement, verified by code + render; the Move dialog is the tested/accessible path — native HTML5 DnD is unreliable to drive in Playwright.)*
- **T-181 — Per-sandbox super-user settings + the folder-creation toggle (ADR-0040).** Settings live on the sandbox row (first setting: `allow_member_folder_create`, default on). Configuration is a super-user act split along the wall — a guest super-user configures a sandbox its own org owns, the owner-super configures any (`canConfigureSandbox`); an ordinary participant never configures. With the toggle off, only a super-user of the sandbox may add folders; ordinary members work within the laid-out structure. `PATCH /sandboxes/:id/settings`; the read carries `allowMemberFolderCreate` + a per-requester `canConfigure` self fact; a Settings modal + gated "New folder" on the surface. No new stored role (composes from `elevated` + `owningOrganisationId`). Migration `0027_sandbox-settings`.
- **T-182 — Create-folder-structure builder (ADR-0040).** A super-user lays out a whole nested tree at once instead of one folder at a time: an indented-outline builder (two spaces / a tab per level) with a live preview, creating the structure in one `POST /sandboxes/:id/folder-structure` (super-user-gated, `canConfigureSandbox`; ≤200 folders). Reusable folder templates (project-/org-level starter structures) are a deliberate **follow-up** — the free-form builder lands first.
- **T-180 — Freeze is a real check-out (ADR-0032 addendum).** The Slice-A honest deviation left Freeze inert (it only locked the head when an internal round opened). Now **every freeze locks the head** — standalone check-out and review-round check-out are one `head_locked` mechanism, two triggers; a plain check-out upgrades to a formal round by freezing again with a lead reviewer, and a redundant plain re-freeze is refused. The lock is on the document, so it is **format-agnostic**: it refuses the manual PATCH, an ambient-history restore, an uploaded-file→text conversion, and soft-delete; the editor canvas goes read-only. **Release** ("check in") is audited both ways on an append-only `sandbox_checkout_events` trail, by the checkout author, the freeze series' lead reviewer, or an elevated super-user — not while an internal round is open (the round's issue/close is the release). New `POST /sandbox-documents/:id/release`; migration `0026_sandbox-checkout-events`.

- **T-187 — New-sandbox wizard: private/shared → organisations → people (ADR-0042, owner feedback).** The single-scope modal becomes a short wizard: step 1 name + Private (my org) / Shared (across orgs, owner-super only); step 2 (shared) pick the organisations; step 3 who has access — everyone in those orgs, or specific people (a checkbox picker). The super-user admits participants **at creation** rather than only afterward. `POST /sandboxes` accepts `organisationIds` / `participantIds` (validated on-project, de-duped, owning-org/creator skipped) and creates the grants alongside the auto-grant.
- **T-186 — Sandbox provisioning is a super-user act + personal sandboxes (ADR-0042, owner feedback).** Creating a sandbox is now super-user-only (`canCreateSandbox`): an ordinary member cannot; a guest-super creates private (own-org) sandboxes; a shared (cross-org) sandbox stays the owner-super's act (ADR-0018). Every participant gets an **auto-provisioned personal sandbox** (named-user, granted to just them, server-created, one per participant via a partial unique index) — created lazily on first sandbox read. The surface hides the create control from non-super-users, labels the personal card and sorts it first. Ordinary members see their personal sandbox + any they're a member of, and create folders (not sandboxes) within. Migration `0028_sandbox-personal`. *(Flagged inference: guest-super confined to private creation — relax the `multi_org` branch if the owner wants any super-user to open shared, but that moves cross-org visibility off the owner.)*
- **T-185 — Folder-structure builder: interactive tree, no whitespace (owner feedback).** The indented-outline textarea (T-182) relied on the user managing two-space/tab indentation, which was fiddly and misparsed. Replaced with an interactive builder: a name field per folder, a **subfolder** button to nest one inside, Enter to add the next folder at the same level, and per-row remove — nesting shown by visual indentation, no whitespace to manage. The API (nested node spec) is unchanged.
- **T-184 — Sandbox selector as informative cards (owner feedback).** The flat chip list becomes a grid of cards, one per sandbox: name, the owning organisation, and whether it is **private** (single-org/team/named-user) or **shared** (multi-org) — a shared card also lists the other organisations in scope. Clicking a card selects it and reveals its folder tree below (unchanged). The list read gains `organisationIdsInScope` (the live org-grants) for the owner/shared display; names resolve client-side from the roster.
- **T-183 — Sandbox version numbering + the ISO 19650 P/C scheme (ADR-0041).** One working series in the sandbox (`v0.1, 0.2, …`, the ambient history; a plain check-out freezes the current working revision under its `v0.x`); `P{NN}` on the first formal issue or promotion (freeze-that-opens-a-round, or promotion — each client round a further P); `C{NN}` the contractual revision issued on client acceptance (a new immutable current Version of the accepted content, since `version_reference` is immutable — retrieval/library/plan/renditions key on `is_current`). The sandbox read carries a `workingRevision` and the ambient history a `v0.x` per snapshot; the sandbox surface shows the working revision on each document row. Updated the freeze (`P{n}`→`v0.x`/`P{NN}`) and promotion (`v{n}`→`P{NN}`) reference generation.

**Slice A2.5 — The TIDP wizard** — ✅ **built 2026-07-25**, from owner feedback. A super-user defines the full deliverable-plan (TIDP) schema, and producing orgs edit their TIDP against it. Owner rulings: **unify** the schema (code fields flagged as segments), **reuse** the appointment tables + add a document-owner, **reuse** `withdrawn` + a reason for removal.
- **T-188 — Unified deliverable schema + default + owner editor.** The coding scheme becomes one unified TIDP schema: each field carries a `type` (text/select/date/person/people/serial), `required`, an `inCode` flag (composes the coded reference) and/or a `role` slot (author/document owner/reviewer/lead reviewer). The code-builder composes from the `inCode` fields (backward-compatible: legacy fields default to code). A **default Infora schema** (ISO-19650-shaped: seven code segments + purpose/suitability/format metadata + the four role slots) preloads when none is saved and is fully editable by the owner-super (change fields, add fields, reorder, reset-to-default). Rebuilt the schema editor around the unified fields.
- **T-190 — Appoint the deliverable team from the plan (bug fix, owner-reported).** The appointment endpoints existed but nothing in the UI called them (only reviewer *confirmation* was wired), so a producer could never appoint a lead author or propose a lead reviewer — and promotion was permanently blocked ("must be bound, with a confirmed reviewer, first"). The deliverable detail drawer's Authoring team / Review group sections become editable: a producing super-user appoints authors (with lead) and proposes reviewers (with lead) via a people picker; the owner confirms proposals in Review, then promotion launches the cycle. Added the missing `grantAuthor`/`grantReviewer`/`revokeAuthor`/`revokeReviewer` client methods; e2e proves promotion unblocks end-to-end.
- **T-189 — TIDP editing (guest-super).** The New-deliverable modal is schema-driven: the code fields build the reference and the schema's metadata fields (purpose/suitability/format…) render as a Details form (required-gated). The deliverable detail drawer gains a **document owner** picker (a single participant of the producing org, informational, amendable — `PATCH /containers/:id/document-owner`) and a **Remove from plan…** action that keeps the container as a record (`state → withdrawn` + free-text reason via `POST …/withdrawal`) with a **Restore** (`…/restoration`). Producing-org super-user only; migration `0029_deliverable-owner-withdrawal`.
- **T-191 — Document metadata card.** Revision and team render read-only from the lifecycle; the editable revision & suitability fields dropped from the form.
- **T-192 — Plan metadata modal.** Schema-driven metadata fields + the deliverable team in one modal.
- **T-193 — Owner sets up the review side from the deliverable drawer.** Reviewer appointment/confirmation reachable where the owner already works.
- **T-194 — Close-as-rejected becomes a deliberate, reasoned act.** A confirm-with-reason flow replaces the bare action.
- **T-195 — Hover explainers for the deliverable-schema columns.**
- **T-196 — Default deliverable schema = the EWR-MWJV seven-segment convention.**
- **T-197 — Self-describing segment codes.** Each code carries its human description.
- **T-198 — Sectioned schema editor + role `required` made real.**
- **T-199 — Schema column hints as a real hover popover.**
- **T-200 — Structured options editor.** Fixes the can't-type-space bug.

**Slice A2.6 — Owner-feedback fixes** — ✅ **built 2026-07-25**, from the owner's walkthrough of the A2.4/A2.5 surfaces: the review-close verdict gate, accept-publishes, and the library made genuinely usable.
- **T-201 — Super-users can rename a planned deliverable's title.**
- **T-202 — A verdict is required to close a review round; accept publishes.**
- **T-203 — Accept feedback + the modal fits the viewport.**
- **T-204 — The Project library — richer, readable, openable.**
- **T-205 — Opening a library document shows the real file, not source text.**

## Moved from the board 2026-08-05 — built parts of part-deferred capabilities

*The board re-cut (Building for V1 / the deferred register) applies the
standing closed-work convention to two slices whose first parts closed weeks
ago but whose records still sat on the live board. Their deferred parts are
register entries on the board; these are the built halves' records, moved
verbatim.*

### The co-authoring slice (A3) — part 1, built 2026-07-26

**Slice A3 — Co-authoring & the editing substrate: Infora as a WOPI host, native Office files co-authored in real Microsoft Office** — 🎯 **designed 2026-07-25 (ADR-0043 + amendments to 0034 / 0036 / 0039 / 0041); P1 ticketed (T-220–T-222 — renumbered 2026-07-25: the drafted T-208–T-210 were already taken by Slice S), P2–P4 coarse until the CSPP / engine track is live.** The sandbox becomes a true SharePoint / iManage-style working area: drop a draft, open it in Word / Excel / PowerPoint, co-author, and have edits sync straight back — files never leaving Infora. The incumbent-validated posture (iManage Work co-authoring; NetDocuments CollabSpaces — both keep files in their own DMS and become WOPI hosts, renting Office co-authoring via Microsoft's CSPP). Infora stays the system of record and the ethical-wall authority; the SharePoint-as-substrate route was considered and rejected (per-org tenancy collides with the cross-org wall — ADR-0043). Grounding is untouched (library-only; the sandbox never grounds).

*P1 — DMS parity (no Microsoft dependency, ship now):* **✅ T-220–T-222 built 2026-07-26** (one verified commit per ticket; api 175/175, e2e 44/44 green). Deviations: rename is **allowed while checked out** (owner-confirmed — a title is author-owned metadata, not canonical content; the T-166 precedent), so only Replace surfaces the head-lock refusal; upload now seeds a genesis ambient revision so a fresh upload reads `v0.1` and the first replace increments to `v0.2`; the `/file` path joins `sandbox-uploads` on the CSRF multipart allowlist (ADR-0044).
- **T-220 — Contracts + API: sandbox document rename + replace-native-file.** Close the two gaps found this session: a sandbox document has no rename path (the PATCH bodies only carry `content` / `authoringMetadata`), and an uploaded file cannot be replaced. Add rename (`title`) — allowed on an unbound document; a bound document's display name stays the container's (ADR-0038). Add `POST /sandbox-documents/:id/file` (multipart) replacing the canonical native file with a new upload of the same format family — writes a new blob + `file_ref`, bumps the working revision; **refused while `head_locked`** (it rewrites canonical content, like the T-122 conversion) and only for `origin='uploaded'`. Durable prior-blob retention is P2 (noted). | *(Deps: T-122, T-166)*
- **T-221 — Surface: rename & replace-file actions in the sandbox drawer.** Per-document row/context actions in the folder view (reusing the T-163 `Modal`): **Rename** (text field) and **Replace file…** (file picker, `origin='uploaded'` only), each surfacing the head-lock refusal cleanly; the row shows format + last-updated. No `window.prompt`, semantic tokens only (the standing A2.1 acceptance tests). | *(Deps: T-220, T-163)*
- **T-222 — P1 acceptance e2e.** Upload a docx → rename it → replace it with a new docx (working revision increments, history shows it) → check out (freeze) → replace is refused while locked → release → replace succeeds. | *(Deps: T-220, T-221)*

### The ontology slice (O) — part 1, built 2026-07-26

**Slice O — The document ontology: classification vocabulary + first-class relationships** — 🎯 **designed 2026-07-26 (ADR-0045; grill session O); Drawer 6 drawn ([data-model.md](data-model.md)); P1 ✅ built 2026-07-26 (T-240–T-244; renumbered from the drafted T-223–T-227, which collided with concurrent UI/polish commits T-223–T-233 — a T-234–T-239 gap is left for other live sessions), P2 coarse until the Engine track is live.** Built on branch `slice-o-document-ontology` in an isolated worktree (the repo had multiple live sessions); one verified commit per ticket, migration 0031, verified against an isolated DB (db 21/21, api 7/7, knowledge 26/26, e2e 7/7 incl. the wall and the plan-surface render). Over the flat library sits a legible model of *how documents relate* (component 5): a Uniclass 2015 / ISO 19650 classification vocabulary the library owner owns, and typed relationship edges between containers. Colocated relational tables, derived not duplicated (ADR-0024/0045) — so the retrieval path gains a **semantic pre-filter** in the same query as the access+state pre-filter (ADR-0022), the lever that scopes a 100k-document corpus before a single embedding is compared. Agent-facing first with a thin confirmation surface (classification an editable field, edges agent-proposed/human-confirmed — ADR-0045 Fork 3). Grounding is untouched (the ontology is metadata and structure, never a grounded corpus — ADR-0011/0021).

*P1 — the ontology substrate + retrieval pre-filter (no Engine dependency, ship now):*
- **T-240 — Data-model Drawer 6 + migration + seed: the classification vocabulary and relationship-edge tables.** Drawn (Drawer 6). Write the migration for `classification_facet`, `classification_term` (hierarchical, currency-by-state), `container_classification` (mutable, agent-proposed/human-editable), `document_relationship` (append-only, propose-then-confirm, currency-by-state). Seed Infora's default Uniclass 2015 / ISO 19650 facets + terms and **copy them per project at creation** (mirror the acceptance-code seed, ADR-0003/0045). Contracts types. | *(Deps: the acceptance-code copy-per-project seed — T-115 precedent)*
- **T-241 — Contracts + API: classify a container; propose / confirm / retire edges.** Set and edit a container's classification per facet (agent-proposed values allowed, human-editable); create an edge (proposed, no effect), confirm an edge (human-confirm → live), retire an edge (currency-by-state, never deleted). Reads: a container's classification + edges; a project's facet/term vocabulary. Access-resolved (component 2) — edges and classification ride the deliverable-visibility pre-filter (Drawer 5); no path resolves its own permissions. | *(Deps: T-240)*
- **T-242 — Retrieval: the semantic pre-filter.** Extend the grounding/retrieval query (ADR-0022/0024) so a scoped retrieval pre-filters by classification facet/term and by edge-connected containers *in the same statement* as the existing access+state pre-filter — the 100k-doc scoping lever; add the classification slice params to `groundedLibrary(slice)`. Structural-only reads (currency / coverage / dependency) answer from the tables with no vector search. | *(Deps: T-240; existing retrieval T-012/T-033/T-054)* **⚠ Note 2026-07-31 — substrate only, no selector.** The SQL pre-filter is built and tested, but nothing populates it: `AssemblyRequest.request` is `{ text, mode }` (contracts), so `classificationTermIds` is unreachable from the gateway and every agent run still scans the project's whole library. Reachable only by calling `groundedLibrary` directly (`retrieval-scope.test.ts`). Wiring it is blocked on **who selects the scope for a given question** — open, Session 6 in the [grill tracker](../grill-sessions/grill-questions.md); [component-4 §3](../architecture/components/component-4-context.md) records the unwired state. Not a defect: an unwired lever is the safe state until the wrong-scope failure mode is answered.
- **T-243 — Surface: classification field + edge confirmation in the Documents / container view.** A container's classification shown as an editable per-facet field (badged "suggested, unconfirmed" when agent-proposed); its relationship edges listed with accept / reject (confirm / retire) actions — the thin confirmation surface (Fork 3). Semantic tokens, no `window.prompt` (standing A2.1 acceptance tests). | *(Deps: T-241; the Documents view T-110)*
- **T-244 — P1 acceptance e2e.** Create a project (default scheme copied) → classify a container against a facet/term → propose an edge between two containers → confirm it (goes live) → a scoped retrieval pre-filters to the classified subset (fewer candidates than corpus-wide) → retire the edge (leaves the record, no longer counts) → the wall negative: an edge into an unshared container is invisible to a non-shared org. | *(Deps: T-240–T-243)*

## Slice Review Surface — the deliverable status page and the cycle status bar *(minted and ✅ built 2026-08-06, one day)*

The first slice cut from **direct owner UI feedback** — two sketches plus ProjectWise reference screens, developed against the model, mocked, approved, ruled and built in one session. Design record: [mockups/deliverable-status-page.html](../design/mockups/deliverable-status-page.html) (owner-approved), **ADR-0051** (the submission acknowledgement gate) and the **ADR-0035 addendum** (distribution-list visibility), both ruled the same day. The navigation the feedback fixed: clicking a reference on the review schedule lands on a **status page** — progress, people, metadata, documents, transmittals — and "Open the review" is a deliberate second step.

- **T-346 — The submission acknowledgement gate (ADR-0051)** ✅ 2026-08-06. `round_state` gains initial `submitted`; a project-scope round opens only when a Participant of the owner organisation acknowledges — recorded who/when **on the round**, after the first cut (on the transmittal) was refused by the append-only trigger and ADR-0051 §2 was corrected to match (the collision is the record: the build defended ADR-0009/0010's invariant against the ADR's own first draft). Sandbox-scope rounds stay created `open`. Migration 0040 hand-written; comment creation already gated on `open`, so the invariant composed for free. API/e2e suites gained the acknowledgement step.
- **T-347 — The cycle status bar** ✅ 2026-08-06. One component, both screens: Submitted → In review → Responding → Complete off stored state only (the T-293 no-timer rule); round chip; optional prior-round compression; the review-period target as a marker never a gate (ADR-0005); no live comment count (ADR-0014). The owner sees "Acknowledge submission" on a submitted round.
- **T-348 — The deliverable status page** ✅ 2026-08-06. `/review/:containerId` is the status page; the round tray moved to `/review/:containerId/cycle` with a back-crumb; the editor's review-response jump deep-links the cycle. Reviewer confirmation moved here from the schedule. People, metadata, versions-with-renditions per the mockup.
- **T-349 — The review schedule onto the UI kit** ✅ 2026-08-06. The last pre-kit review screen: raw inputs → `TextInput`, Card-table → kit `Table`, retired token names gone; proposal state stays visible on the schedule, the confirm act lives on the status page.
- **T-350 — The transmittal & acknowledgement history** ✅ 2026-08-06. `GET /containers/:id/transmittals` with the ADR-0035-addendum three-way cut enforced in row construction (owner: full distribution + ack state; receiver: own rows; producer: recipients withheld) — dated contracts.md note records why the cut is the endpoint's, never a client filter. Status-page history card renders it; `roundState` distinguishes awaiting-acknowledgement from pre-gate rounds.
- **Acceptance:** `pnpm run check` green at every ticket; review-path e2e green (slice-a 7/7 incl. the browser click-through to the status page, pdf-review, editor-review, plan suites); the wall negative unchanged.

## Slice Walkthrough — the DMS walkthrough rulings become build *(minted and ✅ built 2026-08-09; T-368 closed 2026-08-09)*

The **second owner-directed slice**, and the first cut from a walk of the *built product* rather than of sketches: the owner read [user-stories-walkthrough.html](../architecture/user-stories-walkthrough.html) — the journey photographed beat by beat — and commented, and the nine numbered rulings (S1–S9) became this slice. Session record, including the ISO 19650 CDE anchoring the load-bearing ruling came from, in [grill-history.md](../grill-sessions/grill-history.md); ADR addenda to **0032 / 0033 / 0038 / 0040**; migrations 0042–0045. `Q-039` was raised by the build (a plan-locked *shared* sandbox derives folder names from the whole TIDP, disclosing its shape to every granted organisation). **S9 grew T-355 in place** rather than taking a new number — its entry stayed with the code-review findings on the board and carries the QA-gate half.

- **T-358 — The schema exports as a fillable Excel template** ✅ 2026-08-09. Teams draft the deliverables list in Excel before a super user touches the plan (S2), so the header row is the schema's own attribute fields and carries **no reference column**: numbering is never drafted in a spreadsheet. Served by the API, not the web bundle — no xlsx dependency existed anywhere in the repo and the dep rules keep one out of the client, so the workbook code landed once, server-side, shared with T-359's parse.
- **T-359 — The plan batch-imports from the filled template** ✅ 2026-08-09. Owner-ruled a **create-only** act (S3): never an amend, never a delete. References are generated by the naming scheme **in file order**, and a reference-like column is ignored. Role-mapped columns are parsed and **dropped with a stated notice** — appointments stay explicit propose/confirm acts (ADR-0033), never a spreadsheet side-effect. T-337's three constraints carried verbatim, including that the file is never corpus and no persisted record echoes its body, because its author/reviewer columns routinely carry **named people** ([personal-data.md](personal-data.md)).
- **T-360 — Org-standard plan columns** ✅ 2026-08-09. The visible column set is the **producing organisation's standard, locked — no personal overrides** (S3), so two members of a firm cannot read different plans. Stored at the `memberships` grain beside `ack_mode`, the existing per-org project-scoped setting precedent; null means the default set.
- **T-361 — The plan row's detail becomes a card** ✅ 2026-08-09. `DeliverableDetail` moved off the right-hand `Drawer` onto the kit's `Modal` (S4). Drawers stay for genuinely lateral context elsewhere.
- **T-362 — The lead author edits their deliverable's row** ✅ 2026-08-09 (ADR-0033 addendum). Row-scoped edit rights became producing-org super users **plus that row's live lead author** (S5), keyed on the `deliverable_authors.is_lead` interval. The lead author edits title, classification and the authoring team, and **proposes** reviewers — a proposal never confirms, confirmation stays the owner's act. Withdrawal, lead-author reassignment and the coded reference stay elevated or super-user acts.
- **T-363 — The structure builder's plan seed** ✅ 2026-08-09. S6's deterministic half, useful alone: a candidate tree from the org's own plan rows' `discipline` metadata, **no model call**, prefilled into the existing builder for the super user to edit and confirm.
- **T-364 — The structure builder's agent** ✅ 2026-08-09. The second embedded assistive agent (ADR-0027 propose-confirm): a free-form ask fills the same builder. The split is **structural, not polite** — there is deliberately no apply endpoint, so the only writer is still the deterministic `folder-structure` POST. Reads no sandbox content (`Q-020` untouched) and writes nothing (`Q-031` dodged as T-337 dodges it). **Three residuals named rather than discovered later:** `Q-034` is brushed (the system prompt carries a little domain judgement in TypeScript); **no Run record** — the call's usage and ADR-0037 §6 egress facts are dropped where every other model path records them, and T-337 should set that pattern first; and a tree proposed in a free mode then switched to plan-locked can leave a manual folder beside an identically-named derived one.
- **T-365 — Plan-locked: the third folder mode** ✅ 2026-08-09 (ADR-0040 addendum, S7). The tree derives from the owning organisation's own plan rows — discipline folder per discipline, working folder per deliverable — and the derived levels are **system-owned**. A retitled row renames its folder; a **withdrawn row keeps its folder, badged off-plan** — nothing deleted, content never orphaned. Inside a deliverable's folder `allowMemberFolderCreate` still governs, so the two settings **compose** rather than replace each other. Switching the mode on **backfills** for rows that already exist. Schema: `sandboxes.plan_locked`, `sandbox_folders.kind` + nullable `container_id`.
- **T-366 — Bind confirms on a card and reads the row through** ✅ 2026-08-09 (ADR-0038 addendum, S8). `BindModal` became a **confirmation card** — reference, the row's title, its schema metadata, the appointments, and the consequence stated before an explicit confirm; a draft sitting in a plan-locked deliverable folder arrives **pre-selected, never silently bound**. And inheritance became visible: a bound document **displays its row's title and metadata by reference over `container_id`** — read-through, never copy — so the sandbox retitle refusal now points at the plan row where the title actually changes (T-362's delegation).
- **T-368 — The walkthrough, recaptured against what the slice built** ✅ **2026-08-09.** Nine rulings had moved the product under the page that provoked them. Recaptured live: 28 beats over six acts (was 18 over five), with the five new beats S1–S9 asked for — the schema screen the story now opens on, the structure builder and its agent, the three-way folder mode beside the QA gate, the plan-locked tree, and the bind card. **The one non-cosmetic change was the gate itself:** default-on QA means the script's bare `promotion` call is refused, so the capture now runs the real freeze → staff → internal round → accept → promote path rather than turning the gate off — which is exactly the beat S9 asked the story to keep, and it earned the page a new act (III, *The organisation checks its own work first*) and a third persona. **Two gap cards were retired as false** — the internal QA round (T-355 built it) and the plan row's drawer (T-361) — and the remaining four were each re-checked against the built code before the narrative was rewritten, rather than assumed. **Two honest findings the recapture surfaced, recorded on the page rather than staged around:** staffing the *first* internal lead reviewer has no surface (the reviewer control is gated to the owner or an existing lead and hard-codes a non-lead grant), so it is now its own gap card; and the internal round's close-and-issue modal still promises the deliverable "enters the project library", which is the wrong sentence on an org-private round — the capture photographs that modal and the beat names the error rather than cropping it out. **The provenance section was rewritten to name every act driven through the API rather than clicked** (world setup, the two staffing acts, the acknowledgements, version two's repeat pass) after a review of the draft found a blanket "every other act is a click" claim that was not true — on a page whose whole claim is that nothing is staged, the disclosure is the feature.
- **Acceptance:** `pnpm run check` green at every ticket; e2e 57/57 against a fresh seed and a restarted substrate after the capture mutated the seeded world. The walkthrough artifact was republished to its existing URL — a new one orphans the link already shared.
